newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia signs gem export quota resolution for 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia signs gem export quota resolution for 1997.

text.p: Russia has signed a resolution outlining rough diamond export quotas for 1997, possibly bringing a long-delayed gem trade deal with De Beers of South Africa closer, a diamond official said on Tuesday.

"We received the government resolution, which was signed on June 27, on Monday," Georgy Minayev, spokesman for Russia's dominant diamond producer, Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS), told Reuters. "I think this step will bring the trade deal with De Beers closer...it will help."
Minayev said exports under the quotas would be slightly lower than in 1996 due to extended delays in getting government permission to deliver the gems abroad.

"I can't give details on the value or size of the quotas. They will be slightly lower this year than in 1996, although not by much," he said. It was not clear if the quotas included gems ARS may be allowed to export outside a trade deal with De Beers.

Russia allowed exports of some rough gems up to the end of May, but a large proportion of those stones was seized by customs officials and are still being held by the state strategic reserve for revaluation.

ARS is now waiting for the government to sign a formal gem trade deal with De Beers. The South African diamond giant sharply curtailed purchases of Russian diamonds at the start of 1997 when Moscow failed to make its position clear on a draft agreement submitted to the cabinet in October 1996. Russia accounted for 26 percent of De Beers' total worldwide sales under the previous gem trade deal, which was worth around $1.2 billion a year to Russia.
